Figure 1. Examples of spontaneous reactions in metabolic pathways. (A) The conversion of glutamic-γ-semialdehyde to pyrroline-5-carboxylate
occurs spontaneously in proline biosynthesis. (B) Spontaneous steps link dopaquinone and 4,5-seco-Dopa to the pigment betalain. (C)
Spontaneous isomerization of oxazoline to isoxazolidinone in siderophore acinetobactin biosynthesis. (D) The enzymes THS and NISO were later
linked to presumed spontaneous transformations in opiate alkaloid biosynthesis.7,8 (E) The chalcone isomerase CHI catalyzes the spontaneous
cyclization of bicyclic chalcone into tricyclic (S)-flavanone.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Structural characterization and mutagenesis study of RohQ. (A) Overall structure of RohQ dimers. (B) Dimeric interface and the amino
acid residues surrounding the bound imidazole molecule. Four Asp residues (D51/D51′ and D70/D70′) are oriented toward the imidazole center,
and two Tyr residues (Y66/Y66′) form π-stacking interactions with imidazole in parallel-displaced conformations. (C) Analysis of
cyclodehydration activity of RohQ variants relative to RohQ-WT. All assays were run in triplicate. (D) Hydrogen-bonding interactions between
W55 and D70′ and π-stacking between W55 and H73′ can be observed in this expanded active site pocket.
